results.corrected_claim: Apple Developer News, "App Store submissions now open for the latest OS releases" (September 9, 2026), verbatim: "Starting April 2027, apps and games uploaded to App Store Connect need to meet the following minimum requirements: iOS and iPadOS apps must be built with the iOS 27 & iPadOS 27 SDK or later / tvOS apps must be built with the tvOS 27 SDK or later / visionOS apps must be built with the visionOS 27 SDK or later / watchOS apps must be built with the watchOS 27 SDK or later". macOS is not on that list. The UIDesignRequiresCompatibility doc says verbatim: "The system ignores this key when you build for iOS 27 or later, iPadOS 27 or later, Mac Catalyst 27 or later, macOS 27 or later, or tvOS 27 or later." The key exists only for iOS, iPadOS, macOS and tvOS (all 26.0+). The WWDC26 Platforms State of the Union says: "We'll be removing support for opting to use the old design. So once your app is recompiled with Xcode 27, it will automatically begin to use the new design with Liquid Glass." So from April 2027, iOS, iPadOS and tvOS uploads can no longer opt out of Liquid Glass, and the checklist should read "Built with Xcode 27+ (iOS 27 SDK), required for uploads from April 2027". Until then the current rule applies (since April 28, 2026: built with the iOS 26 SDK or later), so "Xcode 26+" is still acceptable today. IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0 is not affected, because Xcode 27 supports iOS deployment targets 15–27.
results.notes: Primary sources: developer.apple.com/news (apple-other); documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/uidesignrequirescompatibility JSON (apple-doc); WWDC26 session 102 transcript (apple-video). Both quotes were re-checked with neutral prompts. The finding goes too far in one place: "Liquid Glass effectively mandatory for ALL App Store submissions". macOS is not in the April 2027 SDK list. watchOS and visionOS do not have the UIDesignRequiresCompatibility key. Adopting Liquid Glass says Liquid Glass changes on watchOS "appear automatically ... even if you don't build against the latest SDK", and visionOS has no Liquid Glass APIs. The finding's facts are verbatim-correct, but its conclusion should be limited to iOS, iPadOS and tvOS (plus Mac Catalyst and macOS only if built with the 27 SDK). The skill line itself is not wrong yet; it becomes outdated in April 2027.

results.corrected_claim: The skill's "Swift 6.1+" is wrong. The minimum toolchain for the Liquid Glass APIs is Xcode 26.0 (iOS 26 SDK), and its compiler is Swift 6.2. Xcode 26 release notes, verbatim: "Xcode 26 includes Swift 6.2 and SDKs for iOS 26, iPadOS 26, tvOS 26, watchOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, and visionOS 26." and "Xcode 26 requires a Mac running macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later." Compiler versions from the support matrix: Xcode 26 and 26.0.1 = Swift 6.2; 26.1 = 6.2.1; 26.2 and 26.3 = 6.2.3; 26.4.1, 26.5 and 26.6 = 6.3 (26.4 itself is not listed). Xcode 27 (also 27.1 RC and 27.2 beta 2): requires macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later. SDKs: iOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS/macOS 27 and DriverKit 27. Deployment targets: iOS 15–27, iPadOS 15–27, tvOS 15–27, watchOS 9–27, visionOS 1–27, macOS 12–27. On-device debugging and simulators: iOS 17+, tvOS 17+, watchOS 10+, visionOS 1+. Compiler: Swift 6.4, with language modes Swift 6, 5, 4.2 and 4. Xcode 27 release notes, verbatim: "Xcode 27 includes Swift 6.4 and SDKs for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, tvOS 27, watchOS 27, macOS 27, and visionOS 27." and "Xcode 27 requires a Mac running macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later."
results.notes: Sources: developer.apple.com/support/xcode (apple-other), plus the xcode-26-release-notes and xcode-27-release-notes DocC JSON (apple-doc). One small inaccuracy in the finding: it says "26.4–26.6: Swift 6.3", but the page lists only 26.4.1 (Swift 6.3), not 26.4. A suggestion for the rewrite: label the row as the compiler version (6.2+ for iOS 26 APIs; 6.4 with Xcode 27). The APIs do not require Swift 6 language mode, since Swift 5 mode is still supported.

results.corrected_claim: Verbatim metadata.platforms for glassEffect(_:in:), Glass, Glass.clear, GlassEffectContainer and PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass: iOS 26.0, iPadOS 26.0, Mac Catalyst 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0. All are non-beta and not deprecated, and visionOS is absent from every one. Declaration, verbatim: "nonisolated func glassEffect(_ glass: Glass = .regular, in shape: some Shape = DefaultGlassEffectShape()) -> some View". Other current declarations: "@MainActor @preconcurrency struct GlassEffectContainer<Content> where Content : View" and "@export(implementation) nonisolated static var glass: GlassButtonStyle { get }". HIG Materials, verbatim: "In visionOS, windows generally use an unmodifiable system-defined material called glass that helps people stay grounded ...". visionOS has its own API instead, glassBackgroundEffect(displayMode:), which is available on visionOS 1.0+ only. So "visionOS 26+" in SKILL.md's platforms/description and in §15 of 01-api-reference.md is wrong for the Liquid Glass APIs.
results.notes: Source type: apple-doc. I fetched swiftui/view/glasseffect(_:in:).json, swiftui/glass.json, swiftui/glass/clear.json, swiftui/glasseffectcontainer.json, swiftui/primitivebuttonstyle/glass.json and swiftui/view/glassbackgroundeffect(displaymode:).json, plus the HIG materials.json (apple-other). The docs are current for the 27 SDK: the @export(implementation) attribute appears, yet visionOS is still not listed. Glass members are still only interactive(_:), tint(_:), clear, identity and regular.

results.corrected_claim: WWDC26 Keynote transcript, verbatim: "On our newer iPhones, iOS already has an advanced CPU scheduler. ... And not only that, but we also figured out a way to bring it to older models, all the way back to iPhone 11. And yes, that does mean that iOS 27 is supported on iPhone 11 and all of the same iPhone models as iOS 26." The iPhone floor for iOS 26 and iOS 27 is therefore the same, iPhone 11-era hardware, and the skill's "iPhone 11 or later" floor is correct. Its parenthetical is not: an iOS 26+ app cannot be installed on older iPhones, and no Apple source describes a system "flat translucent material" fallback for older devices. The parenthetical should be removed.
results.notes: Source type: apple-video (WWDC26 session 101 "Keynote"). The quote was re-checked with a neutral prompt and the surrounding context matched. iPhone SE (2nd/3rd gen) support rests only on secondary sources and on search-engine snippets of Apple Support's "iPhone models compatible with iOS 26/27" pages. support.apple.com, www.apple.com and web.archive.org were all blocked or unresolvable from this environment, so that part stays secondary, as the finding says. The SE (2nd gen) uses the same A13 chip as the iPhone 11 and came out after it, so "iPhone 11 or later" is consistent with it.

results.corrected_claim: WWDC26 Platforms State of the Union, verbatim: "To maintain exceptional readability, we tuned Liquid Glass so it more effectively diffuses complex content behind it. And to establish more depth and separation, we also introduced a darkened edge along with brighter specular highlights. We also made it more personalizable with a new slider in settings to adjust Liquid Glass anywhere from ultra clear to fully tinted ... Apps already using Liquid Glass get these improvements automatically when they run on this year's releases without even needing to recompile." Keynote, verbatim: "To ensure exceptional readability, we tuned Liquid Glass so it diffuses complex content behind it much more effectively, while also creating more depth and separation." WWDC26 "What's new in SwiftUI" (269), chapter summary: "Apps automatically adopt the updated Liquid Glass appearance on 2027 OS releases without code changes." The HIG Color sentences are verbatim-correct ("For smaller elements like toolbars and tab bars, the system can adapt Liquid Glass between a light and dark appearance ... Liquid Glass appears more opaque in larger elements like sidebars to preserve legibility over complex backgrounds ..."), but they are iOS 26-era guidance from the December 16, 2025 HIG update, not an iOS 27 change.
results.notes: Sources: WWDC26 sessions 102, 101 and 269 (apple-video), re-checked with neutral prompts; HIG color.json and developer.apple.com/design/whats-new (apple-other). Caveats: "darkened edge" and "brighter specular highlights" appear only in the State of the Union, not in the Keynote. Apple says "this year's releases" or "2027 OS releases" without naming platforms, so limiting the availability to iOS/iPadOS/macOS 27 is the finding's narrowing, not Apple's. The HIG Materials page was last updated September 9, 2025 and does not yet describe the 27 changes. The State of the Union also says sidebars "expand to the edges on Mac and iPad", and that macOS 27 supports the "show borders" environment value.

results.corrected_claim: Confirmed from primary sources. HIG Materials, verbatim: "The appearance of these variants can differ in response to certain system settings, like if people choose a preferred look for Liquid Glass in their device's settings, or turn on accessibility settings that reduce transparency or increase contrast in the interface." Adopting Liquid Glass, verbatim: "For example, people can choose a preferred look for Liquid Glass in their device's settings, or turn on accessibility settings that reduce transparency or motion in the interface." Neither names a location, a version, or Clear/Tinted values. For iOS 27, the Keynote says verbatim: "Since everyone's preference varies, we're adding a new slider and settings to adjust Liquid Glass, so you can set it anywhere from ultra clear to fully tinted. ... And for developers who have already adopted Liquid Glass, these customizations apply in your apps right away." The State of the Union says "a new slider in settings to adjust Liquid Glass anywhere from ultra clear to fully tinted", and session 269 says "Liquid Glass has a refined look and automatically responds to the new Liquid Glass slider to adjust its tint." Not verifiable from primary sources: (a) that iOS 26.1 introduced a binary Clear/Tinted option; (b) that it lives in Settings > Display & Brightness > Liquid Glass; (c) the iOS 27 location. The skill's "Settings → Accessibility → Display" and "opacity multiplier" wording have no support in any Apple source I found. Apple describes a clear↔tinted look, and in iOS 27 a slider that adjusts tint.
results.notes: Sources: WWDC26 sessions 101, 102 and 269 (apple-video); HIG materials.json and technologyoverviews/adopting-liquid-glass.json (apple-doc/apple-other). The iOS & iPadOS 26.1 and 27 developer release notes do not mention the setting. support.apple.com ("About iOS 26 Updates" 123075, "What's new in iOS 27") is blocked by proxy policy (403/ENOTFOUND), as are www.apple.com and web.archive.org. Search-engine snippets and many secondary outlets (Tom's Guide, Macworld, PhoneArena, Apple Community) consistently describe 26.1 as Clear vs. Tinted under Display & Brightness, but these are secondary. "iOS 27 replaces it with a slider" is an inference: Apple says it is "adding a new slider and settings" and does not say the 26.1 choice was removed.
